projectBackground.name: Liquidity Review — Alder Industrial Group
projectBackground.context: Alder pays suppliers in euros and receives dollars. The CFO wants to know if there is enough cash and how exposed the group is.

manager.name: Anya Moser
manager.note: Cash is the one number that can't be restated. Forecast it honestly and keep a buffer.

assignment.title: Forecast liquidity and manage exposure
assignment.brief: Build the cash forecast, compute FX loss and interest on surplus and advise the CFO.

documents.name: Cash Position
documents.note: Opening cash 500; receipts 320; payments 410 (thousands); minimum buffer 300.

documents.name: FX Receivable
documents.note: €200,000 receivable; booked at 1.10 USD per EUR.

tasks.title: Closing Cash
tasks.prompt: Opening 500, receipts 320, payments 410 (all in thousands). What is closing cash?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Surplus Over Buffer
tasks.prompt: The minimum buffer is 300 thousand. What surplus is available (thousand)?
tasks.mistake: Investing the buffer risks a liquidity gap.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: FX Loss
tasks.prompt: A €200,000 receivable was booked at 1.10 USD per EUR. If the rate falls to 1.05 and it is unhedged, what is the loss (USD)?
tasks.reasoning: Unhedged exposure loses when the currency falls.
tasks.mistake: Treating FX as noise ignores real cash impact.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Interest on Surplus
tasks.prompt: 110,000 invested for 90 days at 3.6% (360-day basis). What interest (currency units)?
tasks.reasoning: Simple interest uses the day count.
tasks.mistake: Using a full year gives 3,960, which is wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Weekly Cash Forecast (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Closing cash in column E = B + C - D for three weeks (thousands). Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: Week 3 hits the minimum buffer exactly: a warning.
tasks.tip: Link next week's opening to this week's closing.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Advice to the CFO
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence recommendation to the CFO on liquidity and FX.
tasks.modelAnswer: Cash falls from 500 to 300 over three weeks, touching our minimum buffer in week 3, so I recommend not investing beyond the 110 surplus and delaying non-critical payments if receipts slip. The euro receivable carries a 10,000 dollar loss at 1.05; I propose hedging 50% with a forward and matching euro payments where possible. We'll update the forecast weekly and escalate if cash approaches 300 earlier.
tasks.reasoning: A good recommendation gives the liquidity picture, an action on FX and triggers.
tasks.mistake: Optimism without a buffer is not treasury.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: Profitable and Bankrupt
caseStudy.background: A profitable manufacturer ran out of cash when a large customer paid 60 days late. It had no weekly forecast and no credit line.
questions: Why can a profitable firm fail?
How large should the buffer be?
caseStudy.solution: Quantis introduced a 13-week rolling cash forecast and a minimum liquidity policy.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Profit is opinion; cash is fact.

options: Rate x principal x days / basis

prompts: How big should your buffer be?
How often would you update the forecast?
